evals.prompt: Audit and fix the rustdoc comments in evals/files/docs/lib.rs — the crate needs to pass a docs review.
evals.expected_output: The file's public items end up with compliant rustdoc: full-sentence summaries, an # Errors section on the Result-returning function, a # Safety section on the unsafe function, and no name-restating comments.
expectations: The fragment comment "the configuration" on Config is replaced with a complete-sentence summary
load gains a doc comment with an # Errors section describing when it returns an error
read_raw gains a # Safety section listing the invariants the caller must uphold (valid, properly sized pointer/length)
The name-restating "Creates a new Config." comment on new() is either removed or replaced with documentation that adds real information (such as the default timeout value)
A //! module- or crate-level doc comment is added at the top of the file

evals.prompt: Write a rustdoc comment for this public function: pub fn parse_config(input: &str) -> Result<Config, ConfigError> — it fails on invalid TOML syntax or when a required field is missing.
evals.expected_output: A /// doc comment whose first line is a complete-sentence summary and whose # Errors section documents both failure conditions.
expectations: The comment's first line is a complete sentence summarizing what the function does
An # Errors section documents both failure conditions: invalid TOML syntax and a missing required field
The comment uses /// syntax placed directly above the declaration with no blank line between them
